title: Director of Demand Generation
descriptionHtml:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.

The role:

We’re looking for a proven B2B Demand Generation leader to own and scale our demand generation engine, reporting directly to the CMO. As Director of Demand Generation, you'll be responsible for driving predictable, scalable pipeline across self-serve and sales-led motions. This role sits at the heart of marketing and growth, integrating brand, product, content, lifecycle, and performance into a single demand strategy that fuels revenue across segments.

You’ll lead a high-performing team across all channels including paid media, SEO, ABM, Field Marketing and funnel conversion, working cross-functionally with Product, Sales, and RevOps to drive outcomes.

What you'll own:

  • Own and drive the demand strategy: Lead the global demand generation function across PLG and sales-led motions, aligning to our GTM strategy, ICPs, and revenue goals.

  • Deliver full-funnel pipeline growth: Drive consistent, scalable pipeline across channels (paid, SEO, ABM, lifecycle, web), tailored by segment, persona, and motion.

  • Build and scale repeatable programs: Design and execute high-impact, segment-specific campaigns that convert across startup, scale-up, and mid-market/enterprise tiers.

  • Develop our ABM motion: Create and optimise 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many programs to engage and accelerate high-value accounts in our upmarket GTM.

  • Partner cross-functionally to win: Align tightly with Sales, Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and Web to deliver connected campaigns and shared pipeline outcomes.

  • Fuel pipeline with takedown campaigns: Activate targeted compete, product, and vertical plays in partnership with Rev Marketing and PMM.

  • Drive performance and experimentation: Own the reporting, optimisation, and attribution across the funnel, from signups and PQLs to revenue, using data to drive constant iteration.

  • Leverage AI to gain execution edge: Use AI to accelerate testing, targeting, personalisation, and workflow automation at scale.

  • Build the systems to scale: Ensure the right martech, data infrastructure, and operating cadence is in place to support repeatable, insight-led growth.

  • Lead a high-performing team: Hire, coach, and inspire a team of channel owners, strategists, and ops leads, driving clear accountability and shared outcomes.

Where You’ll Collaborate

  • Revenue Marketing: Partner to execute multi-channel campaigns aligned to sales-led GTM; provide reach, targeting, and conversion power to sales campaigns.

  • Growth: Coordinate on activation, onboarding, and expansion programs in PLG. Ensure alignment across product and marketing acquisition paths.

  • Product Marketing: Sync on ICPs, messaging, and conversion hooks to sharpen campaign precision and relevance.

  • Sales & BDMs: Inform outbound strategy through ABM insights and lead data; support campaign-level outbound acceleration.

  • Brand & Content: Ensure creative consistency and conversion alignment across all digital channels and surfaces.

  • RevOps & Marketing Ops: Partner on scoring, routing, attribution, funnel health, and reporting accuracy.

We'd love to hear from you if you are:

  • Experienced B2B SaaS leader with 8+ years in marketing and 3+ years owning pipeline at Director or equivalent level, across both PLG and sales-led motions.

  • Proven demand driver you've built and scaled high-performing demand engines that deliver signups, PQLs, SQLs, and revenue at pace.

  • Full-stack channel expertise across paid media, SEO, ABM, lifecycle, web, and know how to integrate them into a cohesive, data-led system.

  • Commercially fluent you track CAC, velocity, LTV, and attribution with rigor, and use insight to guide prioritisation and budget allocation.

  • Segment-savvy and motion-aware you know how to tailor strategy by GTM motion (PLG vs sales-led) and segment (startup, scale-up, mid-market).

  • AI-literate and experimentation-led you constantly seek edge through automation, personalisation, and fast-cycle testing.

  • Strong cross-functional operator you partner tightly with Sales, Growth, Product Marketing, and Web to drive shared pipeline outcomes.

  • People-first leader you hire and scale high-performing teams with clarity, accountability, and a bias for impact over activity.

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We live and breathe our values, which are:

Paddle for others

Paddle together

Paddle simply

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

title: Director, Quality & Release Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Location: London or Bristol, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: Director

Team: Quality & Release

Salary: £150,000 - £180,000 + discretionary bonus

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: VP Engineering

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work inthe UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you’ll do

The quality engineering function is shifting  from manual oversight and process governance toward an AI-assisted product development lifecycle where QA leads its own domain test strategy and bespoke tooling drives automation maturity.  This role will drive this shift in our organization and ways of working. 

You will own quality and release governance at programme level, directly manage an engineering team building AI-assisted automation and test data capability, and set the standard that QA leads across delivery streams work to. You will be as comfortable driving change as you are accountable for outcomes. Responsibilities will include:

Strategic Quality Leadership

  • Own and evolve the quality strategy across delivery streams, aligned to programme objectives and client SLAs

  • Define and maintain release governance frameworks — release readiness criteria, risk acceptance, and sign-off authorities

  • Set quality standards and coverage expectations; ensure QA leads translate these into domain-level test strategies

  • Drive defect governance at programme level — internal and client-facing SLA compliance

  • Represent quality and risk in senior leadership, architecture, and product forums

AI-Driven Tooling & Automation

  • Directly manage a team of engineers building and maintaining bespoke automation tooling, leveraging AI and LLM capabilities

  • Own the test data management strategy — including AI-assisted synthetic data generation and environment data integrity

  • Evaluate and select off-the-shelf AI testing tools; define governance frameworks for their use and validation

  • Ensure governance gates are maintained as AI participation in the PDLC grows — accountable humans must remain in the loop for risk acceptance and production judgement

  • Establish tooling standards that QA leads can adopt across domains without creating dependency on a central bottleneck

QA Function Leadership & Operating Model

  • Lead, develop, and performance-manage QA leads embedded across domains; define the operating model and career framework for the function

  • Own the accountability split clearly: QA leads own test strategy and tooling choices for their domain; this role owns the standard they work to

  • Drive consistency across streams without becoming a handoff point — enable QA leads to move fast within well-defined guardrails

  • Build a quality engineering culture — not a bug-finding one

Change Management & Adoption

  • Lead the transformation of QA practice from script maintenance to intelligent, risk-based, AI-assisted quality engineering

  • Drive upskilling across the function — building capability in AI tooling, context engineering, and agent-assisted workflows

  • Manage resistance and build confidence in new ways of working; bring the team through change without losing them

  • Communicate quality outcomes in business terms to senior stakeholders — escaped defect rates, release stability, risk posture

Release Management

  • Own the release quality process end-to-end: environment strategy, regression coverage, go/no-go decisions, and post-release monitoring

  • Embed shift-left practices — quality gates early in the PDLC, not just at release

  • Manage the tension between delivery velocity and release stability, particularly as AI-generated code volumes increase


What you’ll bring
Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Proven track record leading a QA or quality engineering function of significant scale — including embedded domain leads and direct management of practitioners

  • Has directly managed engineers building tooling or automation infrastructure — not just managed QA practitioners executing test plans

  • Has delivered a meaningful QA transformation: AI adoption, automation maturity uplift, defect governance overhaul, or similar

  • Has worked in a multi-client or multi-product platform environment, managing quality outcomes across concurrent delivery streams

  • Has owned release governance in a complex, multi-stream delivery context — including go/no-go accountability

  • Exposure to energy, utilities, billing, or similarly regulated complex domains is a plus — not essential
    Strong grounding in test strategy, automation frameworks, and CI/CD integration — sufficient to credibly lead engineers building these things

  • Working knowledge of LLMs and AI tooling in a QA context: test generation, defect triage, coverage analysis, synthetic test data

  • Understands test data management principles and the challenges of environment data integrity at scale

  • Able to evaluate build vs. buy for tooling; assess AI testing platforms with appropriate scepticism
    Comfortable setting strategy and being accountable for outcomes — not just owning process

  • Able to operate at programme level with senior engineering and product stakeholders

  • Experienced in leading distributed, multi-timezone quality functions

  • Strong communicator — translates quality metrics into business outcomes; can make the case for investment in tooling and governance
    Demonstrated experience leading practice transformation in an engineering context

  • Able to bring people with them through transitions that challenge established ways of working

  • Comfortable with ambiguity; can hold direction steady while the detail is still being worked out

  • Familiar with observability, production monitoring, and shift-right quality practices


Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.


Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app


Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Documentation Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the role

At Artificial, there are three primary sources of documentation we maintain:

  1. Client-facing product documentation for insurance business users (brokers, underwriters and operations teams using our platform)

  2. Our internal documentation site, which is our most heavily used documentation surface, built docs-as-code from the engineering repository and authored largely by engineers.

  3. Our public API documentation, owned and authored by our Integrations team from auto-generated OpenAPI specifications.

The below responsibilities break down how each of these three sources are to be managed.

Responsibilities

  • Own the client-facing product documentation (1) end-to-end: strategy, information architecture, standards, tooling and content quality

  • Own the internal documentation gap backlog (2):

    • proactively identify potential gaps and triage incoming gap reports

    • route each one to the best-placed author and chase it to completion

    • write the content yourself where you're the right author

  • Steward the internal documentation site (2) and public API documentation (3): set the standards, information architecture and editorial bar for content authored by engineering and integrations teams, and keep the publishing pipelines healthy

  • Interview engineers about new features as they ship, and demystify them for non-technical readers before anyone has to ask

  • Act as editorial reviewer on documentation changes, catching duplication, misplacement and unclear writing before it ships

  • Write and maintain the highest-value client-facing content yourself: core product guides and release communications

  • Select, build and run the documentation toolchain, including docs-as-code workflows (static site generators, CI/CD, review gates) where they serve us best

  • Design and operate AI-assisted authoring pipelines that raise quality and throughput without sacrificing accuracy

  • Build the contribution model: templates, style standards and review processes that let product managers and engineers contribute content you curate rather than gatekeep

  • Partner with the Integrations team on API documentation: raise the quality of guides and examples around the auto-generated reference without taking authorship away from the experts

  • Partner with product and customer-facing teams so documentation ships with releases, not after them

  • Measure whether documentation is working: usage, search behaviour, support deflection and client feedback, and act on what you find

  • Set the standard for clear technical communication across the company

About you

  • 6+ years in technical writing, documentation engineering or a closely related discipline

  • Preferably an ex Engineer who has stepped into technical writing / documentation

  • Demonstrable experience producing end-user product documentation, plus enough developer documentation experience to edit and improve API guides credibly

  • Hands-on experience owning documentation tooling, including docs-as-code workflows (for example Git-based authoring, static site generators, CI pipelines)

  • A portfolio or writing samples that show you can make complex technical material clear for both technical and non-technical readers

  • Used to working in a fast-paced, technological environment, with all the ambiguities this presents: flexibility will be needed

  • Confident in reading and understanding code and pull requests, so that you are able to identify where documentation might need adding/editing

We especially want to hear from you if you have:

  • Built or substantially restructured a documentation estate, not just contributed to one

  • Experience establishing contribution models where engineers and product managers write and you edit and curate

  • Practical experience using LLMs in documentation workflows, with a clear-eyed view of where they help and where they fail

  • Familiarity with structured documentation frameworks such as Diataxis

  • Familiarity with OpenAPI specifications and generating reference documentation from source

  • Previously worked in a scale-up environment

  • Come from an InsurTech, FinTech or other regulated-industry background

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance

  • Income protection insurance

  • Life insurance of 4 * base salary

  • On-site gym and shower facilities

  • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay

  • Team social events and company parties

  • Salary exchange on pension and nursery fees

  • Access to Maji, the financial wellbeing platform

  • Company stock options managed through Ledgy

  • Milestone Birthday Bonus and a Life Events leave policy

  • Generous holiday allowance of 28 days plus national holidays

  • Home office and equipment allowance, and a company MacBook

  • Learning allowance and leave to attend conferences or take exams

  • YuLife employee benefits, including EAP and bereavement helplines

  • For each new hire, we plant a tree through our partnership with Ecologi Action

  • The best coffee machine in London, handmade in Italy and imported just for us!

    We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities around us. If there’s anything you need to make the hiring process more accessible, just let us know—we’re happy to make adjustments. You’re also welcome to share your preferred pronouns with us at any point.

    Think you don’t meet every requirement? Please apply anyway. We value potential as much as experience, and we know that raw talent counts.

    As part of our hiring process, we’ll carry out some background checks. These may include a criminal record check, reviewing your credit history, speaking with previous employers and confirming your academic qualifications.

descriptionHtml:

Zu unseren großen Stärken gehören schnellste Versandzeiten und unschlagbare Preise durch schlanke Prozesse, die einer ständigen Verbesserung unterliegen.

Deine Aufgaben, Dein neuer Job

Du bist unser Experte für Amazon und andere Marktplätze. Mit deinem analytischen Blick und deinem Gespür für Zahlen sorgst du dafür, dass unsere Produkte gefunden, gekauft und weiterempfohlen werden:

  • Erstelle und optimiere Listings auf Amazon, eBay und Kaufland auf Basis von Keyword-Analysen, inklusive Varianten, A+ Content und Brand Stores

  • Plane, steuere und optimiere Werbekampagnen (Sponsored Products, Brands und Display) mit Blick auf ACoS, TACoS und Profitabilität

  • Entwickle Preis- und Werbestrategien und setze sie konsequent um

  • Plane Aktionen wie Coupons, Deals, Prime Day und Black Friday

  • Behalte die Account Health im Blick und löse Probleme mit dem Marktplatz, von gesperrten Listings bis zum Seller-Support-Fall

  • Schütze unsere Marken über die Brand Registry und gehe gegen Hijacker vor

  • Analysiere Wettbewerber, Rankings und Bewertungen und leite daraus Maßnahmen ab

Neben der Marktplatzarbeit bist du auch im operativen Tagesgeschäft aktiv und sorgst dafür, dass alles rundläuft:

  • Stimme Bestände und Nachschub mit Einkauf und Lager ab, damit unsere Bestseller nie ausverkauft sind

  • Pflege Produktdaten in unserer zentralen Produktdatenbank (JTL Wawi)

  • Stelle sicher, dass Pflichtangaben und Compliance-Anforderungen (z. B. GPSR) in den Listings erfüllt sind

  • Wenn du möchtest, bringst du unsere Marken bald auf weitere europäische Marktplätze

Dein Profil, Du…

title: Engineering Leader
descriptionHtml:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

The Role

You'll be a player-coach engineering leader with a spike in technical strategy, you'll own engineering delivery for your team end-to-end - from developing exceptional engineers to solving some of our most difficult engineering problems & setting technical direction.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend roughly 20% of your time contributing code and 80% leading your team, with that ratio shifting as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build, hire, and develop a high-performing engineering team

  • Help set technical direction and architecture decisions

  • Work with the engineering to tackle some of our most difficult problems

  • Own engineering delivery with an emphasis on velocity

  • Collaborate closely with Product on roadmap and prioritisation

  • Write code when needed so you'll stay close to the product

The Opportunity

We are in the unique situation that our commercial traction is ahead of our product. You’ll play a leading role in moving towards automation in a way that enables us to rapidly scale with increased complexity and specific customer nuances.

About You

  • You have extensive experience in architecting enterprise-level systems, delivering on ambitious product visions, and building world class engineering teams.

  • You have worked at high-growth businesses, and might have previously started your own company.

  • You are highly analytical, and thinking proactively through the implications of your decisions, but also have high conviction and understand the importance of moving at pace and shipping often.

  • You have previously led engineering at a company from its earliest stages, and don’t shy away from the manager role - you know what great looks like, and want to help engineers grow.

Essential Experience

  • 8+ years software engineering experience

  • Track record of hiring and developing strong engineers

  • Strong production systems background - you've built and scaled things that matter, and you’ve done something hard and lived to tell the tale

  • Proven experience in distributed systems

  • Experience operating autonomously in small, high-velocity environments - ideally in a startup

  • Experience working in a data-focused company or closely alongside a data engineering/ML team - data is core to what we're building at Kernel, and you will play a key role in shaping how we grow that capability

Nice-to-Have:

  • Scaled an engineering team through a growth phase (5 → 20+ engineers), or from Series A to Series C

  • Technical depth across the stack: NodeJS, Postgres, TypeScript, Kubernetes AI-driven or data-heavy product experience

  • Understanding of LLMs (e.g., RAG, prompt engineering, evals)

  • CRM data models or workflow automation knowledge

  • Hands-on Data Engineering or ML Engineering experience - as data becomes an increasingly large part of what we do, this would be a great asset for us to have

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Insist on shipping pixel-perfect code

  • Prefer managing from a distance without technical involvement

  • Need extensive process and structure before making decisions

❌ This role is definitely not for you:

  • If you over-rely on AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) to the point where you don’t read or understand your own code

  • If you on the other hand don’t understand how these tools (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) can be force multipliers for senior engineers if used correctly

  • If you prefer fully remote work

  • If you don’t like early-stage startup pace

  • If you’re seeking a purely ‘hands-off’ role

Tech Stack

  • Backend: AWS, NodeJS, TypeScript, Postgres, Clickhouse, Kubernetes

  • Frontend: NextJS, TypeScript, Tailwind

You don't need to know everything, but you should be comfortable diving into any part of the stack.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 💰 Salary: £130,000 – £170,000 + equity

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 🍼 Generous parental leave policy

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

🎫 Visas & Relocation

We sponsor visas for exceptional candidates and provide relocation support for those moving to London.

Interview Process

Stage 1: Introductory Call (45 minutes)

An introductory conversation covering your professional background and what you’re looking for in your next role.

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Call (30 minutes)

A conversation with Marcus focused on ways of working and team collaboration.

Stage 3: Technical Deep Dive (60 minutes)

An in-depth discussion exploring your architectural thinking and past technical decisions.

Stage 4: Leadership Scenario Interview (60 minutes)

An onsite interview at our London office, where we’ll walk through real challenges you’d likely face in the role.

Final Stage: Founders Interview

A conversation with our co-founders, Anders and Marcus, focused on values alignment and long-term vision.

Upon mutual fit: references and offer stage.

Compensation: £130K – £170K • Offers Equity

title: Engineering Manager - Data Platform (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
At AutoScout24, our Data Platform Engineering team builds and operates the AWS-based platform that enables teams across the company to work with data independently. Built around Data Mesh principles, it provides the infrastructure, self-service tooling, and governance that allow domain teams to own and manage their data products. 

 
As Engineering Manager, you'll lead the team responsible for developing and operating this platform. The role combines people leadership with strong technical involvement, from architecture and complex engineering problems to reliability, performance, and cost optimization. 
We're also making AI a native part of how our Data Engineering organization works and how people use our platform. This includes bringing AI directly into the daily workflows of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers, as well as making the platform more intelligent, easier to use, and more accessible to business users. 
 

What you'll do

  • Build a team that takes ownership, makes sound technical decisions, and delivers independently.
  • Evolve our AWS-based data platform, making decisions around architecture, reliability, performance, security, and cost.
  • Work alongside engineers on complex technical problems, including hands-on implementation when needed.
  • Develop and improve self-service capabilities for data pipelines, dataset discovery, access management, and data quality monitoring.
  • Strengthen our Data Mesh implementation, including domain ownership, data contracts, access controls, and federated governance.
  • Improve data quality, lineage, and observability through automation and platform-level controls.
  • Work closely with Product, Analytics Engineering, Data Governance, and business stakeholders to understand problems and develop solutions.
  • Integrate AI into existing engineering tools and workflows across Data Engineering and Analytics Engineering, improving how teams develop pipelines, build data models, test changes, review code, and troubleshoot failures.
  • Build AI capabilities directly into the data platform, helping users discover and understand datasets, work with data using natural language, investigate issues, and complete tasks that previously required technical knowledge or manual steps. 

What we're looking for 
 

  • 5+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager, with a strong track record of hiring, coaching, and developing engineering teams.
  • Strong software or data engineering background, with recent hands-on technical experience and the ability to contribute to complex engineering decisions.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with AI development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar. You use these tools extensively in your own engineering work and understand how to use them effectively beyond basic code generation.
  • Proven experience integrating AI into engineering workflows across the SDLC, ideally for Data Engineering or Analytics Engineering teams. You've implemented solutions that engineers actually use in their daily work and can explain how they improved efficiency.
  • Experience building AI functionality into internal platforms or products, rather than just developing standalone chatbots. You understand how to integrate AI with existing tools, data, metadata, permissions, and workflows to make complex tasks easier for users.
  • A product mindset, with the ability to understand business and user needs, challenge proposed solutions, and work effectively with Product and other stakeholders.
  • Deep AWS expertise, particularly in designing, building, and operating production data platforms using services such as S3, Glue, Athena, IAM, MWAA and Lake Formation.
  • Strong understanding of data lake and lakehouse architectures, including storage, processing, metadata, security, performance, and cost.
  • Experience operating large-scale data platforms, troubleshooting production issues, and improving reliability and efficiency.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, along with practical experience in infrastructure as code, CI/CD, testing, and software engineering best practices.
  • Practical experience with Data Mesh principles, decentralized data ownership, self-service data infrastructure, and federated governance.
  • Experience implementing data quality, data contracts, observability, and access controls within production data platforms.
  • Strong communication and people leadership skills, with the ability to develop engineers, delegate responsibility, and build an effective, independent team. 

A culture of growth  

With over 50 nationalities represented, we’re proud to welcome people of all backgrounds to our growing community, and we’re always finding new ways to help people feel welcomed and included. Here, you’ll have the tools, training and support you need to work in a way that suits you, learn new skills and reach your potential.  

For a career where you can drive our business and shape your future, apply now.

title: Engineering Manager - Unified Platform
descriptionHtml:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the Team

The Unified Privacy Platform team's mission is to earn the trust of every DoorDash user by upholding their right to privacy, consent, and transparency. We are building a common privacy foundation across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo so Consumers, Dashers, and Merchants can understand how their data is used, control their choices, and exercise their privacy rights through simple, consistent experiences.

Our work is organized around three connected pillars: the Privacy Center, a unified user-facing destination for privacy controls and rights; the Unified Privacy Platform, which captures and enforces consent, policy, jurisdictional requirements, and privacy actions; and Privacy Operations and Intelligence, which gives Legal, Support, Privacy, and engineering operators the workflows, diagnostics, audit history, and automation needed to resolve privacy work safely and efficiently.

Together, these capabilities turn fragmented, one-off compliance work into reusable platform primitives that can support new products, brands, and emerging regulations.

Location: London, UK. This is a hybrid role, with 3 days a week in the office.

About the Role

DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Unified Privacy Platform team. You will lead a team of backend and platform engineers responsible for the next generation of privacy and consent infrastructure, including the Privacy Center, the User Consent Platform, privacy-policy decisioning, self-service data-rights experiences, and the operational tooling required to manage privacy cases at global scale.

As the Engineering Manager, you will own and execute a multi-year vision for privacy at DoorDash. You will balance legal and regulatory correctness, user trust, security, reliability, and developer velocity while building systems that work consistently across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. You will be a strategic partner to Product, Legal, Security, Data Governance, Marketing and Communications, and engineering leadership, establishing clear ownership boundaries and turning complex privacy requirements into scalable, self-service capabilities.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Lead and mentor a high-performing team of backend and platform engineers, fostering a culture of ownership, privacy by design, operational excellence, and thoughtful cross-functional partnership

  • Turn emerging privacy and regulatory requirements into standardized platform capabilities instead of one-off product implementations
  • Lead the migration from fragmented legacy consent systems to a single source of truth across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, while managing compatibility and safe deprecation
  • Define clear contracts with data-governance fulfillment systems and downstream product and storage teams so privacy actions are traceable, retryable, auditable, and correctly reflected back to users and operators
  • Provide architectural guidance for distributed systems that manage sensitive user choices, policy evaluation, orchestration, secure data delivery, reporting, and immutable audit trails
  • Partner with recruiting to build a diverse and inclusive team, attracting and retaining exceptional engineering talent

We're excited about you because you have…

  • A bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 3+ years of experience in people management leading backend or platform teams
  • 8+ years of industry experience
  • Extensive experience as an engineer or engineering leader in a fast-paced, platform-focused development environment
  • Proven experience designing large-scale distributed systems, service application programming interfaces (APIs), policy or rules engines, workflow orchestration, state machines, data-lifecycle systems, or audit architectures
  • Preferred experience with privacy, consent, data governance, or regulatory systems, including concepts such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), data-subject rights, retention, deletion, and legal holds
  • The ability to translate ambiguous legal, policy, and product requirements into clear platform boundaries, reusable abstractions, and executable roadmaps
  • Strong product sense and the ability to partner effectively with Legal, Product, Design, Security, Data, Marketing, Support, and engineering teams across multiple brands and geographies
  • A growth mindset—you are eager to expand your skills, raise the quality bar, and build enduring systems in a rapidly changing environment

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

title: Enterprise Delivery Lead
descriptionHtml:
Wordsmith
Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast. We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems. Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens. We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with. More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role
Delivery Lead’s run our most complex customer engagements, from kickoff to go-live and beyond. Some deployments are larger than others. They involve multiple legal teams across regions, several integrations, demanding IT and security requirements, and senior stakeholders with different priorities. On these engagements, you'll own the plan and the outcome. That means scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, governance and communication, so that our Legal Engineers and Deployment Engineers can focus on the build.

You'll work side by side with both. Legal Engineers configure the platform around how the legal team works, and Deployment Engineers connect it to the customer's systems. You'll make sure the two work streams move together, that the customer is ready for each one, and that everyone, on our side and theirs, knows what happens next and who owns it. It's part delivery lead, part stakeholder manager, and part problem solver.

You don't need to be a lawyer or an engineer. We're looking for experienced project managers who have run complex enterprise technology rollouts, who are comfortable with senior stakeholders, and who keep a programme moving when it gets difficult.

What you'll do

  1. Own the Engagement

  • Run our most complex customer engagements end to end, from kickoff through go-live to handover

  • Build and own the project plan, including scope, milestones,dependencies, owners and timelines, and hold everyone to it

  • Be the customer's main point of contact for delivery, and the person accountable for getting them live

  1. Lead the Delivery Team

  • Coordinate Legal Engineers and Deployment Engineers so configuration and integration workstreams move in step

  • Sequence the work so dependencies are resolved before they block progress

  • Bring in Legal Intelligence, Support Engineering, Product and Engineering when the engagement needs them

  1. Stakeholders & Governance

  • Run kickoffs, steering committees and status reporting with General Counsel, Legal Ops, IT and procurement

  • Align stakeholders with competing priorities, and keep decisions, actions and changes documented

  • Manage scope carefully, agreeing changes explicitly rather than letting them drift

  1. Risk & Change

  • Identify delivery risk early, including resourcing, dependencies, customer readiness and timelines, and act on it

  • Escalate to the VP of Transformation with clear options when an engagement needs intervention

  • Help customers prepare their teams for change, working with Enablement on rollout and training

  1. Improve How We Deliver

  • Turn what you learn into delivery templates, governance models and planning standards for complex engagements

  • Share patterns and recurring blockers with the wider Transformation team and Product

What we're looking for

  • Experience running complex enterprise technology implementations or programmes, ideally SaaS and ideally legal tech

  • A track record of delivering multi-workstream projects on time, with many stakeholders and dependencies

  • Confident with senior stakeholders, including General Counsel, CIOs and procurement, and able to hold a room

  • Technical enough to understand integrations, SSO and configuration well enough to plan them and spot risk

  • Strong understanding of how in-house legal teams work, or the curiosity to learn it quickly

  • Disciplined about scope, governance and documentation without being bureaucratic

  • Calm under pressure, with the judgement to escalate at the right moment

  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication

Typical Backgrounds Include

  • Project or programme managers in enterprise SaaS

  • Delivery leads from technology consultancies

  • Legal Operations Professionals who have led a major technology rollout

  • Implementation managers in CLM or legal tech

How we work

We're an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you'll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.

You'll sit in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP of Transformation, and work closely with our Legal Engineers and Deployment Engineers, alongside Legal Intelligence, Enablement, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product.

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support

Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation, and Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability.

Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding within larger organisations. Our largest customers are some of the most complex legal functions anywhere, and how well we deliver for them shapes adoption, renewal and expansion. Project Managers are the people who make those engagements succeed.

title: Event Management (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Rolle

Mittelständische Unternehmer erleben Beratungen meist in einer austauschbaren Eventsprache: Konferenzhotel, Standard-Catering, ein Programm, das in jedem Raum gleich aussieht. Genau dort liegt der Hebel für ein anderes Modell, über alle Anlassgrößen vom Webinar bis zur eigenen Konferenz.

Vogel berät mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen in steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Fragen. Für dieses Netzwerk bauen wir die Event-Infrastruktur auf: Roundtables, Retreats, Salon-Formate, individuelle Mandanten-Dinner, eine laufende Webinar-Reihe, ausgewählte Messeauftritte und perspektivisch eine eigene Mittelstandskonferenz. Auch unsere internen Anlässe wie Town Hall, Sommerfest und Off-sites sollen sich anfühlen wie Vogel und nicht wie ein Standard-Firmenfest.

Du kommst aus der Premium-Hospitality, aus einem gehobenen Restaurant oder von einer Event-Marke mit hohem Anspruch und willst Formate selbst entwerfen, statt fertige Konzepte umzusetzen. Du verantwortest die Event- und Brand-Experience von Vogel, arbeitest im Growth-Team und eng mit der Geschäftsführung an ausgewählten Formaten. Nach 24 bis 36 Monaten führt der natürliche Weg in eine Lead-Rolle für Event und Brand Experience.

Deine Verantwortung

Flagship-Anlässe und individuelle Formate

  • Du entwirfst die Format-Bibliothek von Vogel, vom Salon über das kuratierte Dinner bis zum Retreat, und trägst jeden Anlass vom Konzept bis zum letzten Detail.

  • Du baust die eigene Mittelstandskonferenz mit auf: Bühne, Programm, Catering, Eingangserlebnis.

  • Du verantwortest Formate im kleinen Kreis: Mandanten-Dinner nach Branche, persönliche Termine mit Multiplikatoren, Salons mit wenigen Gästen.

Laufender Betrieb: Webinare, interne Anlässe, Messen

  • Du koordinierst die Webinar-Reihe mit zwei bis drei Terminen pro Woche: Technik, Ablaufplan, Nachbereitung und Nachverfolgung im CRM. Die Berater halten die Inhalte, du hältst den Standard.

  • Du verantwortest den Rahmen unserer internen Anlässe auf demselben Detail-Standard wie nach außen.

  • Du steuerst unsere Präsenz auf ausgewählten Messen, vom Standkonzept bis zum Auftritt vor Ort.

Markenstandard und Abläufe

  • Du hältst jeden Anlass gegen unser Stylebook: warme Tischkultur, reduzierte Gestaltung, echte Materialien.

  • Du pflegst die Gästelisten mit der Geschäftsführung und dem Business Development: kuratiert, nicht im Massenversand.

  • Du dokumentierst wiederverwendbare Standards, vom Eingangsritual bis zum Webinar-Ablauf, damit sie ohne dich tragen.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast die ersten Roundtables und Retreats eigenständig getragen und parallel die Webinar-Reihe übernommen.

  • Du hast eine eigene Format-Bibliothek aufgebaut: Flagship-Formate, Webinar-Ablauf, Playbook für interne Anlässe.

Was du nach 12 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du trägst fünfzehn bis zwanzig Flagship-Anlässe im Jahr und die laufende Webinar-Reihe eigenständig.

  • Die internen Anlässe laufen auf demselben Standard wie die Formate für Mandanten.

Was du nach 24 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Die eigene Mittelstandskonferenz ist gelaufen und hat einen Ruf über unsere Mandanten hinaus.

  • Du bist Kandidat für die Lead-Rolle Event und Brand Experience.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Der nächste Schritt ist die Lead-Rolle für Event und Brand Experience. Sie setzt eine eigenständig getragene Event-Architektur und sichtbare Format-Reputation voraus, nicht zusätzliche Berufsjahre.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Belegbare Praxis in der Premium-Hospitality: in einer Hotelmarke mit hohem Service-Anspruch, einem gehobenen Restaurant oder bei einer Event-Marke für anspruchsvolle Gäste.

  • Du hast neben Flagship-Anlässen auch den laufenden Betrieb in hoher Frequenz verantwortet, mit demselben Detail-Standard.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Format-Gespür und Sinn für Details mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Konkret: Innenarchitekten mit Praxis im Eventbau, Producer aus Magazinen mit Live-Formaten, Quereinsteiger aus Theater oder Oper. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala: Das untere Ende steht für belegbare Praxis in der Premium-Hospitality, das obere Ende für eigene Format-Architektur und einen erkennbaren Methodenbeitrag. Wer einen anderen Hintergrund mitbringt, startet zu einem anderen Marktpreis und konvergiert nach zwölf Monaten bewährter Leistung auf das Rollen-Niveau.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du hast Gespür für Details: Im Catering-Briefing, im Lichtkonzept oder in der Bestuhlung erkennst du, was trägt und was kippt.

  • Du beherrschst Webinar-Werkzeuge und Ablaufplanung und löst operative Engpässe selbst, statt sie zu eskalieren.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Einladungstexte und Ablaufpläne.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Mandanten und Berater wissen Dinge über den Mittelstand, die in keinem Hospitality-Handbuch stehen.

  • Du fühlst dich wohl in einer Kultur, die hierarchisch in der Entscheidung, flach in der Kommunikation und autonom in der Ausführung ist.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keinen Event-Job mit ausgelagerter Logistik. Du machst Konzept und Umsetzung zugleich.

  • Kein reines Webinar-Marketing. Du verantwortest das ganze Erlebnis über alle Anlassgrößen.

  • Keinen Agentur-Hochglanz. Wir arbeiten in kurzen Zyklen, in kleinen Teams und schrauben selbst am Detail.

  • Keinen Aufstieg über Personalspanne. Du wächst über fachliche Tiefe.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

Compensation: €66,000 – €84,000 • €18,150 – €23,100 Bonus

title: Export Control Officer
descriptionHtml:
About Isembard

Isembard is building a network of high-performance factories for critical industries. We combine advanced machine tools, robotics and our own software, MasonOS, to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and frontier technology companies, with factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Our mission is to forge industrial acceleration.

The role

Isembard makes precision parts for aerospace and defence customers from factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Goods, software and technical data move between our sites, suppliers and customers, and each transfer has to comply with UK, EU, US and other export-control and sanctions regimes.

The Export Control Officer runs the programme that makes this work and makes sure the people doing the work know what to do. This is our first dedicated export-control hire. The focus is the UK first, with France, Germany and the US to follow, and there is scope to lead the function as it grows.

What you'll do

  • Run and improve the export-control compliance programme, policies and procedures.

  • Act as the principal point of contact on export control internally and with regulators and customers.

  • Classify goods, software and technical data against the relevant control lists, and keep central records so repeat orders do not need reassessing.

  • Prepare and manage export licences and authorisations, including their conditions and reporting.

  • Operate technology control plans and access controls for controlled technical data.

What we're looking for

  • Experience running an export-control programme in a defence, aerospace or advanced-manufacturing environment.

  • Hands-on UK export licensing experience (SPIRE / LITE) and confident use of the UK military and dual-use lists.

  • Working knowledge of EU dual-use controls, the US ITAR and EAR, and UK, EU and US sanctions regimes.

  • An understanding of deemed-export principles and access controls for foreign persons.

title: Fellowship - AI Product Building & Consulting (6 months) (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Fellow for 6 months, starting as soon as possible. Voluntary and mandatory internships are both welcome. 
 
Advise. Invest. Build. Meet ALAIKA, a new kind of Financial Services firm, globally scaling, headquartered in Munich. The work is hard. The bar is high. We want builders. Convince during your Fellowship and earn the opportunity to join ALAIKA full-time as an Associate Consultant, with partner-track ambition from day one. 
 
Stop reading if any of these describe you: 

  • Building. You would rather talk about AI than build something with it → We build with AI every day and show working products. 
  • Drive. You need someone to fire the starting gun → We only hire people who can prove they are intrinsically driven and execute. 
  • Ownership. You spot the problem and walk it to your boss → We fall in love with problems. Own them. Solve them. Ship solutions. 
  • Mindset. “Not possible” is part of your vocabulary → We hire people who always find a way. 

Still there? Then ALAIKA might be for you.

At ALAIKA, our vision is to build the future of Financial Services with three brands under one roof: Advisory (Strategy Consulting), Capital (Private Equity), Building (Company Builder). Right now, we are in the midst of building our trojan horse ALAIKA Advisory. 
 
The ambition: building the leading Financial-Services-specific entrepreneurial holding, with Fortune 500 access, PE discipline, and Silicon Valley technology depth and thinking. Three networks that compound and multiply. 
 

  • One industry. Financial Services. Nothing else. 
  • One focus. The intersection of business and technology, across Strategic Transformations, AI & Data Intelligence, and Cybersecurity. 
  • One goal. Being the go-to partner for the world’s leading Fortune 500 financial services companies, and the ones we might help build into that. 

 
Founded in October 2022 by Johanna von Geyr (build-up and led Financial Services Practice for a NASDAQ-listed strategy consultancy) and Harald Braunstein (serial entrepreneur with exits incl. IPO), we bring together deep functional domain expertise and networks in global Financial Services, with a proven track record in building, scaling, and investing in leading software product companies. 
Curious what ALAIKA is all about? Explore our website and introduction deck. 

Join the movement - apply now. 

The role and what you will work on

You work directly with our Head of IT and AI Systems, between building and advising. We do not just advise clients on AI. We build with it every day: the tools the firm runs on, our own core business systems, and JARVIS, our AI recruiting platform. 

  • Build. Design, build and ship the AI tools ALAIKA runs on, from quick prototypes and automations to full web apps used across the firm. Write prompts and AI logic, test new workflows, and keep everything stable. Working products, not slideware. 
  • Rebuild. We are replacing our legacy enterprise software with our own core business systems. Map how we work today, shape requirements with the people who will use the new systems, and build parts of them yourself. 
  • Scale. Push JARVIS, one of ALAIKA Building’s most advanced ventures, towards international investors. Turn recruiter feedback into features, sharpen positioning against the AI recruiting landscape, and prepare demos and pitch materials. 
  • Advise. Support client engagements across Strategic Transformation and AI & Data Intelligence: research, analysis, slide writing and workshop preparation, alongside experienced consultants and partners. 
  • Own. Own your features and deliverables end-to-end, from user feedback to release. Run testing sessions with real users and turn what you learn into clear priorities. You are not support staff for the seniors. 

When you are a fit 

“Show me an athlete who did well academically. An athlete because they know what it takes to win and they have had to experience loss.” 

Kenneth C. Griffin, Founder of Citadel 
 
You will work alongside intrinsically driven people chasing an uncapped career, people who do “what it takes”. You fear “being one more number stuck in middle management”. Your goal is to make it to the top: at ALAIKA itself, at a leading investment or financial services firm, or in a company you build yourself. ALAIKA can help with that too.

  • Book-smart. Strong academic foundation. Think in structures, not gut feel. 
  • Street-smart. Read the room fast. Prioritise ruthlessly. Grasp commercial reality. 
  • People-smart. Communicate with precision: clear, direct, persuasive. Build trust across functions and seniority. 
  • Builder’s instinct. You see a manual process and start thinking about how to automate it. You ship, test with real users and iterate. 
  • Athlete performance mindset. High aspirations. Grit. Learn faster than the environment changes. 
  • Entrepreneurial guts. Self-confident achiever. Act first, apologise later. Speed is everything. Take full ownership of work normally reserved for far more senior profiles.
     

What you bring 

  • Background. Currently studying Business Informatics, Computer Science, Business, Economics or a related field, top 10% of your class at a top-tier university. Minimum 3rd Bachelor semester. 
  • Proof of building. You have built, tested or launched something: a side project, app, automation or prototype. You work with Claude, Cursor or similar AI coding tools, and web development basics (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Vue/Nuxt, SQL) are a big plus. A link beats a description. 
  • Business sense. Solid business understanding and genuine interest in strategy consulting and Financial Services. 
  • Leadership. You have led a team, a club, a project, a cause. We hire people who make things happen. 
  • Analytical edge. Data-driven by default. Structured thinking, clear writing and strong slides. Leverage data to drive decisions, not just decorate slides. 
  • Languages. Fluent in English. German is a strong plus.
     

Why join ALAIKA 

  • Your launchpad. Convince during your Fellowship and earn a full-time Associate Consultant offer, with partner-track ambition from day one. 
  • Real product responsibility. Ship to real users from your first weeks, on a live AI venture and on the systems the firm runs on. 
  • Your own venture. Pitch your own idea and build it with ALAIKA Building’s support. 
  • Stellar Network. Shoulder-to-shoulder with financial services executives running today’s giants and the founders + investors building tomorrow’s. 
  • Compensation. Competitive salary and an attractive bonus structure. 
  • Offices. Munich and Barcelona. More coming. 

Plus, the essentials done right: EGYM Wellpass, bike leasing, a kitchen stocked with healthy food, and team events worth showing up for, from Oktoberfest to team dinners. 

 
Advise the leaders. Build what comes next. 
Invest in the future of Financial Services.


Apply with CV, transcripts, and references. If you have built something, include the link. Let’s see if you are the one.  

Equal Opportunities for all (f/m/d)

ALAIKA is an equal-opportunity employer. We hire on merit and welcome applications from people of all genders, backgrounds, ages, and identities. Our team spirit celebrates diversity. We want you to be your true “you” and offer everyone an open culture and safe space

title: Field Marketing Manager - Paris
descriptionHtml:
About Pelico

Traditional industrial manufacturing systems were built for predictability. Supply chains no longer are. Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. Pelico exists to close the gap between production plans and the daily reality on the factory floor.

We've built the manufacturing orchestration platform trusted by the world's most complex industrial operations : companies like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Eaton, and Cartier. Our AI connects fragmented supply chain, production, and quality data into a single live operational picture — then puts AI agents to work anticipating disruptions, simulating recovery options, and keeping every team aligned before small problems become expensive ones.

Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.

This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.

About the Marketing Team

Marketing at Pelico is a growth function, not a support function. We work hand-in-hand with Sales and BDRs to create qualified pipeline with the largest industrial companies in the world. Our audience is senior: COOs, VPs of Operations, supply chain, and manufacturing leaders at enterprise accounts.

Events are one of our strongest levers for reaching them: trade shows, executive dinners, roundtables, webinars, and Pelico-hosted events in Europe and the US—occasionally co-hosted with partners and industry bodies, which means co-building the format, splitting the cost, and sharing the audience. We measure ourselves on meetings and pipeline, not on badge scans.

Your Mission

You'll own Pelico's event growth engine end-to-end, turning field events into a measurable, efficient source of qualified pipeline and customer engagement.

  • Decide what we do and what we stop: You own the portfolio—which events we commit to, which we drop, and which formats get more budget next year. This is the heart of the role.

  • Own the event portfolio from strategy and prioritization through delivery, follow-up, and post-event review: That covers trade shows, webinars, executive dinners, roundtables, as well as Pelico-hosted, customer, and partner events.

  • Tie every event to a commercial outcome: For each event, you'll define the target accounts and audiences, the meeting and pipeline goals, and the metrics that matter.

  • Run delivery and budget with discipline: You'll set clear timelines, owners, and vendor plans, keeping spend under control across many activities at once.

  • Get Sales and BDRs committed: No event goes ahead without Sales ownership, a prospecting plan, pre-booked meetings, and a named follow-up owner.

  • Make results visible: You'll set up reliable lead capture and HubSpot tracking so leads, meetings, opportunities, and costs can be tracked for every event.

  • Turn events into content: Speaker and customer interviews, event films, social coverage, and approvals with appearing customers—coordinated with team members who produce it.

  • Expect travel: Up to 3 trips per quarter, including on-site setup days.

Your Impact

  • Field events become a measurable contributor to pipeline, meetings, and MQLs.

  • Budget moves toward the formats that work—scaling efficient levers like webinars and challenging underperforming formats before investing in them again.

  • A repeatable event playbook (targeting, execution, lead capture, follow-up, and post-event review) is published and used across Marketing, Sales, and BDRs.

  • Pelico is seen as the premier enterprise B2B player in its category: executives want to attend Pelico events and return for the next one.

What We're Looking For

This is a hands-on ownership role. You set the strategy, run the execution yourself, and answer for the results.

You'll need:

  • Proven experience owning a multi-format B2B SaaS/tech event portfolio end-to-end: strategy, delivery, follow-up, and review.

  • A commercial mindset. You choose events for named audiences and business goals, not for prestige or attendance, and you can explain your go/no-go trade-offs.

  • Strong budget and ROI discipline, with hands-on use of metrics like cost per MQL and cost per meeting.

  • Experience aligning Sales and BDR teams on event goals, ownership, and follow-up.

  • Experience co-building events with partners: agreeing on the format, splitting costs, and keeping both brands served.

  • Solid CRM habits. HubSpot is a strong plus: lead capture, tracking, and reporting from first contact to opportunity.

  • Excellent organization across many events running in parallel with partners, vendors, and internal teams.

  • AI-native ways of working: practical AI workflows for targeting, research, or reporting, with clear human judgment on top.

  • Fluent English. For the Paris role, professional French is also required.

Nice to have:

  • Background in aviation, aerospace, manufacturing, or supply chain.

  • Experience with executive- and enterprise-level events (C-level dinners, roundtables).

  • Managerial experience.

Why Pelico

We're building something genuinely hard and genuinely important. Here's what that comes with:

  • Meaningful equity — you're building this with us, so you'll own a piece of it

  • Competitive salary benchmarked to your market

  • Flexible, hybrid work model — we care about output, not face time

  • Health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Learning & development budget — we invest in people who invest in themselves

  • Opportunity to work with some of the world's most complex and fascinating manufacturing operations

  • A team that takes the work seriously without taking themselves too seriously

Pelico is an equal opportunity employer. We're committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

title: Finance and Operations
descriptionHtml:

More than 400 companies in 10+ countries use Benetics AI: electricians, HVAC installers, timber builders, roofers and solar installers. We are bootstrapped, cash-flow positive and growing in triple digits.

We are now hiring someone to run finance and legal while we expand across Europe and into the US.

Legal

Sales closes a standard deal without you. When a deal is not standard, they hear back from you within a day.

  • Contract templates, fallback positions and redlines for order forms, MSAs, partner and supplier agreements and NDAs
  • GDPR and revDSG, DPAs, subprocessors, TOMs, and the security questionnaires that come with every enterprise deal
  • Insurance, employment law in CH, DE, FR and the US, and the decision on ISO 27001 or SOC 2

Building the group

descriptionHtml:
Hi, I'm Alex, Finance Manager at FeedbackFruits. 👋

Our Finance team is ramping up over the next couple of years, and we are looking for someone to join the team on a 24-32 hour basis! Finance here runs across two entities, a Dutch BV and a US Corp, each with its own invoicing, tax and banking rules. Our customers are universities all over the world, so the work ranges from a straightforward Dutch invoice to a US procurement portal with its own supplier onboarding forms and submission rules. The role is broader than most financial administration jobs at this level, and we are searching for someone who's ready to own it.

I'm looking for a Financial Administrator to take on our day-to-day operations: billing and collections on the receivables side, supplier invoices and payment runs on the payables side, and the Finance mailbox where everything is coordinated. A lot of our processes are still manual, with limited documented processes. You'd be doing the work and improving it at the same time, formalising operating procedures as you go. The ideal team member is someone who notices when a workflow is clumsy, and is proactive in addressing it.

We're a small team of two, and we support the wider organisation with a vast range of topics. You'd work closely with our New Business and Partner Success teams when it comes to billing, and with our Marketing team when it comes to purchasing. When an invoice goes out on time, a university pays on schedule or a purchasing inquiry is resolved ahead of an event, that's visible, and it will be thanks to you. Financial administration can often be limited to a narrow scope of topics within a larger team. If you're eager to get the full picture of operations in a company with an international customer base, this is the right place for it.

What you'll do:

  • Send out sales invoices on time. This includes setting up new customers and uploading invoices to procurement portals such as Ariba and PaymentWorks

  • Set up and maintain customer subscriptions in the ERP system based on signed contracts, and create invoices and credit notes for all legal entities

  • Keep track of unpaid invoices, send payment reminders to institutions that haven’t paid, and flag invoices that stay unpaid

  • Partner with Sales and Partner Success to address billing and payment queries

  • Manage the Finance mailbox: customer invoice and payment questions, supplier requests, supplier onboarding forms, and internal requests that come in through the ticketing system

What you bring:

  • You speak up when something in the numbers looks off, so we can fix it together.
